Definition: Overall cohort: 152 genomes. Primary reference-group comparisons: 144 genomes (23 subflava, 114 perflava, 7 flavescens). Eight species-unresolved genomes are descriptive only.
Local intervals are merged insertion-sequence, integron and provirus predictions. Whole-contig geNomad plasmid-like and viral predictions are summarized separately at the genome level.

A cluster qualifies if at least one member CDS meets ≥1 bp or ≥50% CDS overlap. All-cluster descriptions and randomization-eligible counts have separate denominators. Four partitions × two thresholds × four scopes give 32 BH-adjusted tests.

1,000 within-contig shifts preserve interval lengths and relative spacing. Non-movable layouts are excluded from observed and null counts. Ratios compare observed to mean null counts; tests are upper-tailed with plus-one correction.
GI intervals and GI/MGE overlap proportions are descriptive. Gene-instance and GI-instance denominators in GI_overlap_summary are distinct from pangenome-cluster denominators.

Kruskal-Wallis tests compare three groups; BH q values cover three endpoints within each scope. reference_groups_144 is primary; ANI_assignment_sensitivity_152 uses ANI-channel assignments (31/114/7). representative_subset_95 retains 95 representative records, not necessarily 95 verified participants.

Coefficients use count ranks, adjusted for assembly class, ln(1+contig count) and genome size. The overall group partial F uses df=2,138. This model does not adjust for phylogenetic or study-source effects.

111 eligible two-sided Fisher comparisons across 37 types are jointly BH-adjusted. All 81 recorded types are included as prevalence data. marked_difference requires q<0.05 and absolute target/rest prevalence difference ≥0.50; unresolved genomes are descriptive only.

All 152 genomes had usable outputs for the listed tools. Zero indicates no qualifying detection; blank inferential cells indicate an untested or unavailable comparison. Inf denotes an unbounded estimate. In Defense_types, c/d are presence/absence counts in the remaining comparison groups.

Primary comparisons use 144 reference-assigned genomes (23/114/7). Participant sensitivity uses 95 selected representative records (11/78/6), not 95 confirmed independent participants. Eight species-unresolved genomes are descriptive only.

Six endpoints (IS, proviruses, plasmid-like contigs, viral contigs, GI count and GI coverage) are tested by Kruskal-Wallis. Rank models adjust for assembly class, ln(1+contig count) and genome size. BH correction covers six endpoints separately within each scope and test family. No pairwise group tests or phylogenetic/study-source adjustment were performed.

Per_genome provirus counts and the new abundance comparisons use final geNomad virus_summary calls (208 total). Local-overlap analysis uses 209 coordinate-verified find_proviruses candidates, including CABFLW010000022.1:83-10458 in GCA_901873995.1, which was not retained in the final viral classification. These are distinct detection scopes.

MOB-suite plasmid-reconstruction results were withdrawn because a defective reference-database index invalidated the calls; the corresponding counts have been removed. Plasmid carriage could not be reliably assessed across the cohort. IntegronFinder outputs were evaluable for all 152 genomes, with no integrons detected; this constant-zero endpoint was reported descriptively and was not tested. geNomad plasmid-like and viral contig counts represent candidate predictions rather than counts of confirmed complete replicons.
